$comment: THE authoritative STAC Browser recipe, and the pin every script and test reads. Freva owns this centrally: no deployment forks it, copies its patches or keeps its own upstream pin. A deployment decides only whether the closed 'stac-browser' component is enabled and which STAC API it points at. Everything about HOW the application is constructed - revision, patches, toolchain, build settings, and the shape of the result - is recorded here and nowhere else. Changing any value is a reviewed source change; see UPSTREAM.md.
name: @radiantearth/stac-browser

toolchain.$comment: The versions the recorded output was produced with. Preparation refuses a major mismatch rather than producing a differently-bundled artifact under the same digests. These are also inputs to the cache key.

patches.$comment: Ordered by filename, applied in that order, from a clean checkout of the pinned commit. Every entry carries a digest, an owner and the condition under which it can be dropped, because a patch nobody can justify is a patch nobody will remove.

series.name: 0001-mount-into-the-portal-host-element.patch
series.why: Upstream mounts on <body> because upstream owns the document. The portal hosts the application inside its own shell.
series.changes: app.mount('body') becomes a mount into #stac-browser-mount, failing closed when the element is absent and releasing any prior instance.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - the STAC route keeps the portal header, navigation and footer
series.removableWhen: upstream accepts a configurable mount target

series.name: 0002-expose-init-for-re-entry.patch
series.why: An ES module is evaluated once per document, so upstream's bare init() at the bottom of main.js runs on the first visit only.
series.changes: Publishes window.STAC_BROWSER_INIT so the portal can re-mount on every later entry to the route.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - leaving and re-entering the STAC route re-mounts the application
series.removableWhen: upstream exports its initializer, or the portal stops using a client-side route for STAC

series.name: 0003-follow-the-host-theme.patch
series.why: Two theme controls on one page is a defect, and writing data-bs-theme from outside repaints only the application's shell - its maps, code blocks and tables stay behind.
series.changes: Scopes the colour attribute to the mount, assigns STAC's own reactive colorMode from the portal's data-theme so its watcher commits to the store, and hides upstream's own toggle while the sync is active.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - flipping the portal theme repaints the embedded application
series.removableWhen: upstream supports an externally driven colour mode that reaches the store

series.name: 0004-do-not-scroll-lock-the-host-document.patch
series.why: The Browse drawer sets overflow:hidden on the host document, which freezes the whole portal, not just the embed.
series.changes: Adds body-scrolling to the offcanvas and namespaces the body class it does set.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - the portal still scrolls while the STAC drawer is open
series.removableWhen: upstream's offcanvas stops locking the document, or the embed moves to its own scroll container

series.name: 0005-open-the-validation-report-in-a-new-tab.patch
series.why: The Source valid/invalid tick links to a route of the embedded application. Following it in place replaces the portal's own page with the report: the visitor loses the shell, and the back button lands them somewhere they did not come from.
series.changes: Keeps the tick and its verdict; resolves the validation route to an absolute URL and opens it with target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer instead of an in-place router navigation.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - the validation control leaves the portal page standing
series.removableWhen: upstream offers a way to open its own routes in a new context, or the report becomes a portal route of its own

series.name: 0006-teleport-the-example-code-modal-into-the-embed.patch
series.why: The search 'example code' modal teleports to document.body by default, which puts it outside #stac-browser - outside everything the containment pass scoped, so it is unstyled and it escapes the mount the embed is supposed to stay inside.
series.changes: Adds teleport-to="#stac-browser" to the modal, which is the same mechanism upstream already uses for its own offcanvas.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - nothing the embed opens renders outside its mount
series.removableWhen: upstream teleports its modals into its own root by default

series.name: 0007-open-the-catalogue-description-expanded.patch
series.why: On a landing page the catalogue description IS the content, and opening it clamped to three lines with a 'Read more' reads as a broken paragraph rather than as a summary.
series.changes: Defaults ReadMore to expanded and sets the measured height on mount. The toggle still collapses and re-expands.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - the description renders in full on load

series.name: 0008-ask-before-fetching-a-third-party-basemap.patch
series.why: Upstream's basemap table fetches tiles from openstreetmap.org and usgs.gov on every document with a footprint. The portal publishes a self-contained artifact under default-src 'none', so those requests were refused and the map drew blank: a broken feature and a console full of violations on every collection and item page.
series.changes: Filters the configured layers to origins the deployment listed in allowedBasemapOrigins, read from the runtime configuration. The default is the empty list, so no third-party request is made unless a deployment asked for one; the same statement puts the origin into the artifact's img-src, and upstream's own attribution metadata rides along with the layer.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - an item with a footprint makes no third-party request and raises no CSP violation
series.removableWhen: upstream makes the basemap set a runtime option, or the portal decides to allow third-party tiles unconditionally

series.name: 0009-place-the-portal-introduction-in-the-catalogue-column.patch
series.why: A portal that embeds a catalogue has something to say about it, and upstream renders a description from the STAC document alone. Rendered through the portal's own pipeline it cannot be a `description` - that field is CommonMark rendered with safe:true - so without a placement it can only be stacked above the application, where it reads as a separate page with the catalogue's toolbar and title beneath it.
series.changes: Adds a widget on upstream's own `view-catalog-meta-start` hook that moves the portal's already-rendered introduction fragment into the top of `section.intro` - the item the metadata row shares with the providers - and puts it back when the view is torn down. Also renders a `logo` on a provider when the host has put one there, and keeps such a provider in the simple list.
series.requiredBy: browser-tests/run.mjs - the catalogue introduction is rendered inside the catalogue's own column
series.removableWhen: upstream renders host-supplied HTML in the catalogue view, or the portal stops introducing the catalogues it embeds

patchedTree.$comment: The complete set of paths the preparation is allowed to have modified after applying the series. Anything else dirty in the checkout - a repository-wide formatter, a stray edit, a partially applied patch - stops the build. index.html is listed because the runtime-config markers are uncommented rather than patched.

build.$comment: Upstream's own no-sourcemap build, with runtime configuration enabled. DYNAMIC_CONFIG makes assets document-relative; historyMode 'hash' keeps a deep link surviving a reload on a plain static server with no rewrite rules and unable to collide with the portal shell's own history fallback.

output.$comment: The shape the prepared tree must have. These are assertions about the result, not instructions for producing it: a build that stops emitting a module entry, or starts emitting a service worker, has changed in a way the adapter cannot absorb silently.
output.$serviceWorker: sw.js is upstream's StreamSaver worker and is part of the download feature, so it is prepared rather than forbidden. It is recorded here because a service worker that calls clients.claim() on the portal's own origin is a wider scope than the embed, and that is a live review question listed in the handoff - not something this refactor decided.

adapterContract.$comment: The reviewed upstream option surface the closed portal adapter is permitted to drive, for exactly this pin. Recorded here so that moving the pin forces the contract to be re-stated and the option list re-read.

expected.$comment: The tree digest a verified preparation from these inputs produces on the recorded toolchain. It is an expectation, not a gate: upstream's bundler is not byte-reproducible across every environment, so preparation reports a mismatch loudly and the portal build still verifies the manifest it was actually given. A mismatch means 'find out why before shipping', not 'stop'.
